items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: I had had a little experience... I was in Carnegie and I heard a banjo upstairs... a fellow in the room said, “Hey, I gotta tell Emerson Brown about you.”... So the next day Emerson showed up to my room and said, “How would you like to come down to Paul Parker’s house tomorrow for a rehearsal?”... A

ctx.x: Torch bearer for the Alumni Jazz Band and traditional jazz in general.

Yes, I came to the hill in 1954 and I had had a little experience playing guitar and ukulele and banjo, just a bunch of kids hacking around, and I got up here and I was in Carnegie and I heard a banjo upstairs the first night and I went up and a kid was playing a tenor. And I said could I play it? And a fellow in the room said, “Hey, I gotta tell Emerson Brown about you.” Who is Emerson Brown? I didn't know and he said, “Well you know we have a jazz band here called the Catatonic Five.” And I said, “Oh, that's…
Oh, how neat. So there were six or seven people in the band at that time?
